title: Generation and rearing of axenic Aedes aegypti mosquitoes
protocol: Make up liver:yeast extract powder in a ratio of 3g liver extract to 2g yeast extract.
Mix 2g liver:yeast extract, 1g agar, and 60 mL distilled water in a Pyrex bottle.
Autoclave the mixture for 1 hour.
Allow the agar mixtures to cool down in a water bath at 55°C (~1 hour).
Pour the cooled agar mixtures into Petri dishes (~20 ml/plate) and allow them to cool.
Wrap plates with parafilm and store at 4°C for up to 3 weeks.
Inoculate two 1L flasks containing 500 mL of LB broth with E. coli and incubate overnight at 37°C with shaking.
Pour the bacterial culture into two autoclaved centrifuge jars, ensuring they are balanced.
Centrifuge the jars for 10 minutes at 16,000 RCF and pour off the supernatant.
Resuspend the bacterial pellets in 20 mL sterile PBS.
Mix the bacterial suspension with LY medium using 40 ml of water as described.
Autoclave the mixture for 1 hour.
Pour agar plates.
Wrap plates in parafilm and store at 4°C for up to 3 weeks.
Obtain a segment of filter paper containing Aedes aegypti eggs that are at least one week old and a maximum of three months old.

Prepare sterilizing reagents in a laminar flow hood: fill two small petri dishes with 70% ethanol, one small petri dish with 3% bleach/0.1% Roccal-D solution, and three small petri dishes with autoclaved DI water; also prepare a large petri dish with PBS.
Place the segment of filter paper in a petri dish containing 70% ethanol using flame sterilized forceps.
Incubate at room temperature for 12 minutes.
Transfer the filter paper to the bleach/Roccal-D solution using forceps.
Incubate for 12 minutes; eggs will detach from the filter paper.
Transfer the detached eggs to a sterile cell strainer.
Transfer the eggs to the second Petri dish with 70% ethanol.
Incubate for 12 minutes.
Transfer the eggs to a plate filled with distilled water.
Transfer the eggs, removing the eggs from the cell strainer, to a final petri dish containing PBS.
Place petri dish containing the eggs in a vacuum oven set at room temperature; apply vacuum pressure at 25 Hg for 15 minutes.
Add 5 ml of sterile DI water to each well of a six-well plate.
Remove the dish from the vacuum oven and transfer individual larvae to each well using a 1000 μl pipette.
Use a sterile 1.8 mL cryovial to create plugs in the agar mixture; transfer one plug to each well containing 5 mL autoclaved distilled water.
Wrap edges of six-well plates in parafilm to decrease contamination risk.
Place plates in a dark incubation chamber to allow mosquito development.
Wrap the plates in aluminum foil if a dark incubator is not available.
Set up a 50 ml glass beaker inside a wide mouth 500 ml glass bottle.
Add a square of mesh over the opening of the bottle.
Place a lid with the centre removed on top of the bottle.
Cover the top with a square of aluminum foil.
Autoclave the bottle and water.
Allow the bottle and water to cool to room temperature.
Transfer pupated mosquitoes from 6 well plates into the 50 ml beaker inside the sterilised bottles.
Add a sterilized cotton pad soaked in filter-sterilized 10% sucrose solution as adults emerge.
Change the cotton pad every 2-3 days.
Place adult mosquitoes in a normal light:dark cycle incubation chamber.
Autoclave all glassware and forceps involved in blood feeding in advance.
Employ a sterile axenic mouse pelt as a membrane for blood feeding.
Perform bloodfeeds using a circulating water bath in a class II biosafety cabinet.
Check sterility throughout the experiment through multiple means.
Maintain a three-step verification protocol for checking sterility.
Discard the experiment if any step fails.
Use liquid LY food to maintain a control group of axenic larvae in the sixth well of each 6-well plate.
Make liquid LY to the same specifications as LY agar, excluding the agar.
Discard the experiment if mosquitoes develop past the L1 stage.
Test a subset of axenic larval and adult mosquitoes for contamination by culturing.
Discard the experiment if any mosquito tests positive for contamination.
Test a subset of newly emerged L4 larvae and adults for contamination through 16S rRNA PCR using primer pairs 27F-1492R.
Discard the experiment if any sample tests positive for contamination.
